candidates.proposedStem: Why does a freely falling water stream typically become narrower with increasing distance below a tap?

candidates.candidateExplanation: Gravity accelerates a falling water stream. For approximately steady incompressible flow, the volume flow rate Q = Av is approximately constant, so a higher speed requires a smaller cross-sectional area.
workedReasoning: Falling stream speed increases due to gravity.
For steady incompressible flow without significant mass loss, Q = Av is nearly constant.
Consequently A decreases when v increases.

candidates.originalStem: A main stream (area 2 cm2; speed 5 m s-1) divides into two equal branches of area 1 cm2 each. Branch speed is:
candidates.proposedStem: A main stream (area 2 cm2; speed 5 m s-1) divides into two equal branches of area 1 cm2 each, with equal volume flow rate through both branches. Speed in either branch is:
candidates.candidateExplanation: The 2 cm² inlet at 5 m/s carries 10 cm²·m/s. Equal volume discharge into two 1 cm² branches gives 2 × 1 × v = 10; hence v = 5 m/s per branch. Equal branch areas alone do not require equal discharge.
workedReasoning: Continuity gives A_in v_in = A_1 v_1 + A_2 v_2.
The new equal-flow assumption gives v_1 = v_2 = v.
Without that assumption, v_1=3 m/s and v_2=7 m/s also conserve total flow.

candidates.originalStem: NBF Example 6.3: Aorta radius 0.8 cm, speed 0.33 m s-1; blood enters 30 arteries each radius 0.4 cm. Speed in each artery is:
candidates.proposedStem: Based on the idealized equal-flow split in NBF Example 6.3: Aorta radius 0.8 cm, speed 0.33 m s-1; blood enters 30 arteries, each of radius 0.4 cm, with equal volume flow through each artery. Speed in each artery is:
candidates.candidateExplanation: For the idealized equal-flow model based on NBF Example 6.3, A_in v_in = 30 A_out v_out, giving v_out = (0.8/0.4)² × 0.33 / 30 = 0.044 m/s. Equal radii alone do not prove equal discharge.
workedReasoning: The printed NBF Example 6.3 contains the 0.8 cm and 0.4 cm radii, 30 arteries and 0.33 m/s inlet speed.
For equal outlet discharge, A_in v_in = 30 A_out v_out.
The revised stem is teacher-authored clarification, not verbatim NBF wording.

candidates.originalStem: One vessel (radius 1 cm) divides into 50 equal vessels (radius 0.1 cm). If initial speed is 0.20 m s-1 and flow is conserved, branch speed is:
candidates.proposedStem: One vessel (radius 1 cm) divides into 50 equal-radius vessels (radius 0.1 cm), with equal volume flow rate through each branch. If initial speed is 0.20 m s-1 and the fluid is approximately incompressible, speed in each branch is:
candidates.candidateExplanation: For steady incompressible flow divided equally among 50 outlets, π(1 cm)² × 0.20 m/s = 50π(0.1 cm)² × v. Therefore v = 0.40 m/s. Equal outlet radii without equal discharge do not uniquely determine individual speeds.
workedReasoning: Continuity gives π(1 cm)² × 0.20 = 50π(0.1 cm)² × v under equal discharge.
Alternatively 25 branches at 0.20 m/s and 25 at 0.60 m/s also conserve total flow, demonstrating ambiguity without equal discharge.
